official.deadline_note: For the published 2026/2027 edition the first-stage application window ran 15 March - 15 May 2026; notification of admission to the interview stage was due by 15 June 2026 and the final Programme I admission decision by 30 September 2026. Dates for the next edition are not yet published; the call has been issued annually each spring since 2006.
official.application_cycle: 2026/2027 academic year - 21st edition of Programme I and 11th edition of Programme II
official.status_note: The published 2026/2027 call closed on 15 May 2026 and final admission decisions were announced by 30 September 2026; the awarding body describes the competition as annual, with the new folder published on the same UW Centre for East European Studies page each spring.
official.tuition_coverage_note: Scholarship holders apply for exemption from tuition fees (by decision of the Rector or relevant university authorities) on an individual basis, with the possible support of the Programme Office; persons fulfilling the conditions referred to in art. 324 para. 2 pts 3-7 of the Act of 20 July 2018 (Law on Higher Education and Science, Dz.U. pos. 1668 as amended) are automatically exempted from tuition fees.
official.funding_period: per month (9 months of the academic year)
benefits: Programme I: monthly scholarship of PLN 1,800.00, paid during the studies and the Polish language course
Programme I: tuition fee exemption at Polish public universities, applied for individually with possible support of the Programme Office
Programme II: monthly scholarship of PLN 2,700.00, paid during the internship and the Polish language course
Admission to Polish public universities outside the statutory admission limit for scholarship holders
Preparatory Polish language course funded for holders who do not yet know Polish at the level required for study

Organisational care, monitoring of the course of studies and information meetings provided by the KK Programme Office; graduates receive a Programme completion diploma and may join the KK Programme Alumni Club
eligibility: Programme I: Belarusian citizens who do not have citizenship or the right of permanent residence in the Republic of Poland or another EU/EFTA/OECD country and who, for political reasons, cannot undertake studies or have been expelled from university and therefore have no possibility to undertake or continue studies in Belarus
Programme I is aimed at Belarusian youth of secondary school age and students repressed for political reasons, in particular persons expelled from higher education institutions
Programme I also applies to graduates of the independent Jakub Kolas High School of Humanities in Minsk

Programme II: Belarusian citizens without citizenship or permanent residence in Poland or another EU/EFTA/OECD state who, for political reasons, cannot continue their scientific activity in Belarus, up to 35 years of age at application, holding a master's or specialist degree (second-cycle or unified studies with thesis defence)
Programme II candidates must not already be studying or training at another Polish public university or research institution
requirements: Conditions for payment: residence in the territory of the Republic of Poland and active participation in classes
Holder must open a Polish bank account and pass its number to the Programme Office within 14 working days of arrival
Holder must supply the Office with copies of the admission decision and, by 15 March (winter semester) and 15 October (summer semester), proof of active student status and a transcript of grades
Holder must supply a copy of current health insurance or a document entitling them to health benefits, on the same dates
Gainful employment is permitted only if it does not interfere with the Programme Regulations and the agreement with the University of Warsaw

Before beginning studies, holders must independently obtain a decision on the recognition of their Belarusian secondary education certificate from the Kuratorium Oswiaty (Board of Education) of their place of residence in Poland
documents: Application for admission to the Programme
Documentary evidence of arrest, detention or conviction (if any)
Document confirming expulsion from studies, or information on the reasons for its absence
Other documents the applicant considers relevant to the Selection Committee (e.g. the study programme followed in Belarus, so programme differences can be assessed)
selection_criteria: Motivation for applying for the scholarship and justification of the chosen field of study: 0-10 points
Previous educational record - secondary school or university grades and scientific, social or organisational achievements (research, publications, event organisation, public activity): 0-5 points
Assessment of the chances of using in Belarus the knowledge and experience gained in Poland: 0-5 points

Programme II gives preference to candidates who can demonstrate academic achievements and/or organisational, social or public activity and involvement in transformation, whose motivation and activities to date are the most promising for future use in Belarus
coverage: Monthly scholarship for maintenance during the studies and the Polish language course (Programme I), or during the internship and the Polish language course (Programme II)

Tuition fee exemption at Polish public universities, granted by rector's decision on individual application, or automatically for persons meeting art. 324 para. 2 pts 3-7 of the Act on Higher Education and Science
Funded preparatory Polish language course of one additional academic year for holders who do not know Polish at the required level

Not covered: the obligation to cover the costs of travel to Poland, to ensure legal stay in Poland (student visa, refugee status or temporary residence permit), to pay medical insurance and the student house, and to pay enrolment and other fees resulting from the course of study rests directly with the scholarship holder
application_method: Download the current Programme folder from the UW Centre for East European Studies website and complete the 'Programme Candidate' questionnaire
Prepare the full document set listed in the folder as a single PDF per document
Send the complete set in one e-mail, in PDF format, to the Programme Office at bialorus.studium@uw.edu.pl
Also complete the online application form linked in the folder (Google Forms link); only candidates who have sent a full set of duly completed documents AND completed the online form are considered
Attend the remote interview with the Selection Committee, scheduled individually at the end of June or early July
official.application_route: E-mail the complete PDF document set to the Programme Office (bialorus.studium@uw.edu.pl) and separately complete the online application form linked in the annual Programme folder - both steps are mandatory
official.study_mode: full-time (studies stacjonarne); changing from full-time to part-time study is not permitted and leads to removal from the list of scholarship holders
official.citizenship_residency: Belarusian citizens who do not hold citizenship or the right of permanent residence in the Republic of Poland or in another EU/EFTA/OECD country
official.international_eligibility: Open to Belarusian citizens only; other nationalities are not eligible
official.subject_or_agency_requirement: No field restriction for Programme I studies (full-time studies at any Polish public university); Programme II internships prioritise research projects in the humanities, social sciences, economic and legal sciences and areas concerning broadly understood transformation
official.research_requirement: Programme II requires an outline of the planned research project in Polish, a concise letter of motivation justifying the chosen project, a CV in Polish with photograph, and a list of publications, achievements and professional projects; holders must agree an annual research programme with their tutor, participate in at least 5 academic classes per week, attend regular Polish classes for two semesters, hold weekly consultations with the tutor, prepare a final thesis in Polish of at least 50 pages and defend it by the end of June 2027
official.duration: Programme I: up to 5 years (first-cycle and/or second-cycle and/or single long-cycle master's studies), extended where the study programme provides for a longer period (e.g. medical studies), plus one additional academic year for the Polish language course; Programme II: may not exceed 1 year
official.description: The Konstanty Kalinowski Scholarship Programme of the Government of the Republic of Poland, under the patronage of the Polish Prime Minister, is implemented by the University of Warsaw - Centre for East European Studies (SEW UW) in cooperation with the Ministry of Science and Higher Education and the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, and is funded by the Ministry of Science and Higher Education. The awarding body presents it as the largest programme in Europe lending assistance to young Belarusians unable to study in Belarus due to their political views, offering full-time studies at Polish public universities (Programme I) and one-year research internships in Polish public scientific and research institutions (Programme II).
official.program_type: Government scholarship programme run by the University of Warsaw Centre for East European Studies: Programme I (degree studies) and Programme II (research internship), plus the 'Solidarni z Bialorusia' element under the same regulation

applicant_utility.summary: This is a Belarus-only solidarity programme, not a general international scholarship: you must be a Belarusian citizen without Polish or other EU/EFTA/OECD citizenship or permanent residence, and for Programme I you must be a school leaver, a repressed student, or someone expelled from a Belarusian university for political reasons. Programme I pays PLN 1,800 per month for up to five years of full-time study at a Polish public university, with a funded year of Polish if you need it, and a funded second year is not on offer for doctoral study. Plan around the annual spring window (15 March to 15 May for the 2026/2027 edition) and expect roughly six months from submission to a final decision, with interviews held remotely in late June or early July. Budget separately for your flight, visa or residence permit, health insurance, dormitory and enrolment fees - the programme explicitly leaves those with you.
applicant_utility.best_fit: A Belarusian school leaver or a student expelled from a Belarusian university for political reasons who wants a full degree in Poland and does not yet speak Polish.
application_readiness_checklist: Collect proof of the political repression itself - an expulsion order, arrest or conviction record, or a written explanation of why no such document exists - because a generic motivation letter cannot substitute for it

Assemble your Belarusian school or university paperwork: graduation documents, evidence of study, transcripts of passed subjects, and the study programme you were following so the committee can assess programme differences
Translate or prepare documents in Polish where the folder requires it, and scan everything to PDF before the window opens rather than during it
E-mail the whole set as one message to bialorus.studium@uw.edu.pl and only then complete the online form - both are mandatory and an incomplete set is not considered
Prepare for a remote interview in late June or early July by mid-May, and secure a stable connection and a quiet slot
Once admitted, open a Polish bank account within 14 working days and start the recognition of your Belarusian secondary certificate with the local Kuratorium Oswiaty before your course begins
common_rejection_risks: Submitting the documents but forgetting the online application form, or the reverse - the programme states that only candidates completing both are considered
Sending the file set in several e-mails or in an editable format instead of one e-mail with PDF documents
Having no documentary trace of repression: the folder asks for evidence of arrest, detention or conviction, or information on why such a document is absent
Applying for a programme that cannot be funded within the five-year cap, which also blocks later changes of university or field of study
Being enrolled or training at another Polish public institution while applying to Programme II, which is expressly disqualifying
Holding citizenship or permanent residence in Poland or another EU/EFTA/OECD state, which removes eligibility outright
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Travel to Poland, the student visa or temporary residence permit, medical insurance, dormitory (student house) fees and enrolment or other study fees are all the holder's own responsibility, as is any cost of living above the PLN 1,800 monthly stipend.
document_audit: Expulsion paperwork is the pivot of the file: if you were expelled, provide the document; if you were not, the folder expects a written explanation of its absence rather than silence
Evidence of study in Belarus, transcripts of passed subjects and your Belarusian study programme are requested separately - graduates often submit only the diploma
The questionnaire asks for passport or temporary identity certificate numbers, so those must be current and valid
Documents for persons expelled from studies must explain programme differences, so bring the Belarusian curriculum, not just a transcript
For Programme II the CV, motivation letter and research project outline must all be in Polish, with a photograph on the CV - an English-only file will not read as complete
After admission you must keep supplying active-student status and grade transcripts by 15 March and 15 October each year, plus a copy of current health insurance, or payments stop
alerts: The 2026/2027 round closed on 15 May 2026 with decisions by 30 September 2026; nothing was open on the official page as of 10 October 2026, and the next call has not been announced
The call has historically opened in mid-March, so watch the UW Centre for East European Studies page from February onwards rather than waiting for a portal to remind you
Tuition exemption is not automatic: it is a rector's decision on individual application, with Programme Office support, and only certain categories are exempt by statute
Payments stop if you are not physically in Poland or not attending classes; suspension longer than two years means removal from the list and repayment of everything paid
Switching from full-time to part-time study, changing university or field without notifying the Office, or taking another public scholarship for Belarusians can all end the award
If you are removed from the list you must repay the total of all payments received in that course of study within 14 days
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: One e-mail with the full PDF document set to the Programme Office plus the linked online form, then a remote interview with the University of Warsaw Selection Committee, then an individual contract with the University before payments begin.
